title: This Ant's Jaws Snap Shut at 140 mph (Fastest Bite on Earth)

scenes.text: This ant's jaws snap shut at 140 miles an hour.
The bite takes 0.13 milliseconds. That's 2,300 times faster than a blink.
Scientists needed a camera running 50,000 frames a second just to see it.
Each jaw hits with 300 times the ant's body weight. Prey is stunned before it can move.
In danger, it fires the jaws at the ground and launches itself over a foot backwards.
For you, that's a 132-foot jump. Powered by your face.

description:
The trap-jaw ant closes its mandibles at 35 to 64 metres a second, up to about 140 miles an hour, in roughly 0.13 milliseconds, the fastest self-powered strike ever recorded in an animal.
UC Berkeley researchers filmed it at 50,000 frames a second: each jaw hits with 300 times the ant's body weight, and the ant can fire its jaws at the ground to launch itself 8 centimetres up and 40 centimetres back, the equivalent of a person jumping 44 feet high.
Which tiny animal do you think has the most ridiculous superpower?
first_comment: The jaws accelerate at about 100,000 g. A bullet leaving a rifle is in the tens of thousands. Would you rather have the bite or the jump?
